objects.description: Utility class grouping common DXF constants. It defines two scoped enums: color (AutoCAD/DXF color indices and special values like bylayer/byblock) and version (DXF file format versions). No instances or methods are required; it serves purely as a namespace-like container.

objects.definition:
enum color {
        black = 250,
        green = 3,
        red = 1,
        brown = 15,
        yellow = 2,
        cyan = 4,
        magenta = 6,
        gray = 8,
        blue = 5,
        l_blue = 163,
        l_green = 121,
        l_cyan = 131,
        l_red = 23,
        l_magenta = 221,
        l_gray = 252,
        white = 7,
        bylayer = 256,
        byblock = 0
    };
objects.description: Enumeration of standard DXF color indices and special color selectors. Defined as a nested enum inside DL_Codes.
DXF format version identifiers as an enumeration nested in DL_Codes. Several preprocessor macros in this header alias these enumerators for common AutoCAD marketing names.

A value-type-like class that encapsulates common DXF entity attributes: layer name, AutoCAD color index, optional 24-bit true color, line weight (width), linetype name, per-entity linetype scale, DXF handle, and a flag indicating model/paper space. Provides constructors and getters/setters for all fields. Color: 0=BYBLOCK, 256=BYLAYER; width: -1=BYLAYER, -2=BYBLOCK, -3=default. Default linetype resolves to BYLAYER if empty. No ownership semantics beyond plain fields.

Class representing a DXF extrusion: a 3D direction vector (entity local Z axis) and an elevation offset of the entity’s XY plane from world origin. Manages an internal heap-allocated double[3] for the direction. Provides constructors (default sets direction to 0,0,1 and elevation 0; parameterized allows custom direction and elevation), getters/setters, and an assignment operator performing a deep copy of the vector values. Destructor releases the allocated array. Note: No user-defined copy constructor is provided; the implicit copy constructor will shallow-copy the pointer, which together with the custom destructor can cause double-free if copies are made. Use with care or avoid copying by value.

objects.definition:
class DXFLIB_EXPORT DL_Exception {}
;
objects.description: Base exception type for dxflib. Empty class used as a tag for exception handling. No data or virtual destructor is defined here; behavior and lifetime are standard for an empty class. Details about throw/ catch usage are not documented in this header.

objects.definition:
class DXFLIB_EXPORT DL_NullStrExc : public DL_Exception {}
;
objects.description: Exception indicating a null or invalid string condition in dxflib. Derives from DL_Exception and contains no members. No additional documentation is provided; inferred purpose from the name.

Exception representing an error related to a DXF group code. Stores the problematic group code as an int. The provided constructor is declared without an access specifier; in a class, this defaults to private, implying it cannot be constructed outside the class as defined here. This may be intentional (constructed via friends or static methods elsewhere) or an oversight. No accessors are provided in this header.
Layer metadata: name, flags (1=frozen, 2=frozen by default, 4=locked), and on/off state.
Block definition header: name, flags, and base point coordinates.
Linetype definition: name, description, flags, dash count, total pattern length, and raw pattern segment lengths pointer.
Text style (font) settings: name, flags, geometry parameters, generation flags, font filenames, and basic font traits.
Point entity coordinates.
Line segment with start and end 3D coordinates.
Construction line with base point and direction vector.
Ray with base point and direction vector.
Circular arc defined by center, radius, and start/end angles (degrees).
Circle defined by center and radius.
Polyline header: vertex counts, mesh dimensions (m,n), elevation, and flags.
Polyline vertex: coordinates and bulge (tan of 1/4 arc angle).
Trace/solid/3DFACE planar quad defined by up to four points and thickness. DL_SolidData and DL_3dFaceData are aliases.
Spline header: degree, counts of knots/control/fit points, flags, and optional start/end tangent vectors.
Single knot value for spline definitions.
Spline control point with homogeneous weight.
Spline fit point coordinates.
Ellipse or elliptical arc defined by center, major axis endpoint vector, axis ratio, and start/end angles (radians).
Block insert parameters: target block name, position, scale, rotation, and array parameters.
Multiline text: insertion, direction vector, box size, alignment and spacing, content, style, and rotation.
Single-line text: insertion and alignment points, size/scale, justification and generation flags, content, style, and rotation.
Parameters for ArcAlignedText (text laid out along an arc). Contains string, font/style, arc geometry, formatting, and flags.
Block attribute entity data; extends DL_TextData with a tag identifier.
Common dimension header: definition/text points, type, text formatting, style, rotation, overrides, and arrow flip flags.
Aligned dimension specifics: two extension points in 3D.
Linear/rotated dimension data: two extension points plus dimension and oblique angles.
Radial dimension specifics: definition point and leader length.
Diametric dimension specifics: definition point and leader length.
Angular dimension (two-line) specifics: four definition points.
Angular dimension (3-point) specifics: two line endpoints and a center point.
Ordinate dimension data: two definition points and a flag indicating X- or Y-type ordinate.
Leader entity header: flags, text box metrics, number of vertices, and dimscale override.
Individual vertex for a leader path.
Hatch header: number of loops, solid/patterned flag, pattern name, angle/scale, and origin.
Hatch boundary loop: declares number of edges making up the loop.
Hatch loop edge: union-like structure describing a line, arc, ellipse arc, or spline edge, plus polyline vertices option.
Raster image entity parameters: reference key, insertion point, u/v vectors, pixel size, and display settings.
Image definition table entry: maps a reference id to an image file path.
Dictionary object header with handle identifier. Details of contents are external to this header.
Dictionary entry mapping a name to a referenced object handle.

Abstract interface class that clients subclass to receive callbacks while parsing a DXF file. Provides virtual hooks for all DXF entities, tables, dictionaries, XData/XRecords, and variables. Also stores current DL_Attributes and a heap-allocated DL_Extrusion helper used to set direction/elevation for entities.

Abstract adapter class that implements DL_CreationInterface with empty virtual methods. Intended to be subclassed by clients to handle DXF parsing events without implementing every interface method. Construction is trivial; destruction is virtual. No resources are owned by this class itself. All add*/set*/end* methods are no-ops by default.

Abstract base class interface for writing low-level DXF constructs. Provides helpers for sections, tables, entities, attributes, handles, and common DXF group-code emissions. Concrete subclasses must implement dxfReal, dxfInt, dxfHex, and dxfString to output to a target (ASCII/binary). Manages unique handle generation via m_handle and tracks version-specific behaviors.

Concrete ASCII DXF writer implementing the DL_Writer interface for emitting low-level DXF records to a text (ASCII) DXF file. It manages an ofstream for output and provides helpers to write group-coded real, integer, hex, and string values. It owns the output stream m_ofile and exposes status/close methods. Construction requires a filename and optional DXF version; lifetime and file management are handled internally. Details of formatting semantics follow DL_Writer contract; specifics not shown here.
Forward-declared interface type that callers implement to receive entities while reading DXF. Only a forward declaration is present in this header; the full definition is not provided here.
Forward-declared writer helper used to emit DXF content. Only a forward declaration is present in this header; the full definition is not provided here.

Main DXF reader/writer class for dxflib. Provides APIs to parse DXF input and emit DXF output, tracking interim group codes, entity attributes, and writer state. Fully defined here with declarations; method bodies are elsewhere. Construction is via default constructor; ownership of any returned DL_WriterA* is managed by the caller as per implementation details not present in this header.

functions.name: DL_Attributes::DL_Attributes
functions.description: Default constructor. Initializes an attribute set with empty layer, color 0, no 24-bit color (-1), width 0, linetype "BYLAYER", linetypeScale 1.0, handle -1, and not in paper space.

functions.name: DL_Attributes::setLayer
functions.description: Sets the layer name for the entity attributes. Empty string is allowed and results in a valid but unnamed layer value.
requirements: layer may be an empty string; it is valid per comments.
Caller must pass a valid std::string reference (cannot be null).

functions.name: DL_Attributes::getLayer
functions.description: Returns the current layer name string.

functions.name: DL_Attributes::setColor
functions.description: Sets the indexed DXF color for the entity.
requirements: color must be an indexed DXF color in the range 0..256 where 0=BYBLOCK and 256=BYLAYER (per comments).

functions.name: DL_Attributes::setColor24
functions.description: Sets the 24-bit true color value for the entity.
requirements: color should be a 24-bit color value in the form 0x00RRGGBB; use -1 to indicate no 24-bit color (per comments and getter semantics).

functions.name: DL_Attributes::getColor
functions.description: Returns the current indexed DXF color.

functions.name: DL_Attributes::getColor24
functions.description: Returns the 24-bit true color value or -1 if no 24-bit color is defined.

functions.name: DL_Attributes::setWidth
functions.description: Sets the DXF line width (thickness) for the entity.
requirements: width may be any DXF width integer; special values: -1=BYLAYER, -2=BYBLOCK, -3=default width (per comments).

functions.name: DL_Attributes::getWidth
functions.description: Returns the current DXF line width (thickness).

functions.name: DL_Attributes::setLinetype
functions.description: Sets the entity's linetype name. The value is not validated against defined linetypes.
requirements: linetype may be any string; no validation is performed (per comments).
Caller must pass a valid std::string reference (cannot be null).

functions.name: DL_Attributes::setLinetypeScale
functions.description: Sets the entity-specific linetype scale multiplier.

functions.name: DL_Attributes::getLinetypeScale
functions.description: Returns the entity-specific linetype scale multiplier.

functions.name: DL_Attributes::getLinetype
functions.description: Returns the linetype name, or "BYLAYER" if the stored linetype string is empty.

functions.name: DL_Attributes::setHandle
functions.description: Sets the DXF handle (identifier) for the entity attributes.

functions.name: DL_Attributes::getHandle
functions.description: Returns the DXF handle (identifier) value.

functions.name: DL_Attributes::setInPaperSpace
functions.description: Sets the DXF code 67 flag indicating whether the entity is in paper space (true) or model space (false).

functions.name: DL_Attributes::isInPaperSpace
functions.description: Returns true if the entity is in paper space, false if in model space.

functions.name: DL_Extrusion::DL_Extrusion
functions.description: Default constructor. Allocates internal storage for a 3-element direction vector, initializes it to (0,0,1), and sets elevation to 0. Use to create an extrusion with default world-Z direction and zero elevation.
requirements: No arguments required.
Object must be destroyed with the destructor; do not attempt to free internal pointers manually.

functions.name: DL_Extrusion::DL_Extrusion
functions.signature: DL_Extrusion(double dx, double dy, double dz, double elevation);
functions.description: Constructs an extrusion with the provided direction components and elevation. The direction represents the entity’s extrusion/Z axis; elevation is the XY plane’s offset from the world origin.
requirements: dx, dy, dz, and elevation are doubles; no normalization is performed.
Inputs should be finite doubles to avoid undefined behavior in downstream consumers.
Object must be destroyed with the destructor; do not attempt to free internal pointers manually.

functions.name: DL_Extrusion::~DL_Extrusion
functions.description: Destructor. Releases the internally allocated direction vector.
requirements: After destruction, the object must not be used.
Callers must not delete or free the pointer returned by getDirection(); it is owned and freed by this destructor.

functions.name: DL_Extrusion::setDirection
functions.signature: void setDirection(double dx, double dy, double dz);
functions.description: Sets the internal 3D extrusion direction vector components. Does not normalize or validate the vector.
requirements: dx, dy, dz should be finite doubles.
If a unit vector is required by the caller’s logic, the caller must normalize before calling this function (not enforced by this API).

functions.name: DL_Extrusion::getDirection
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the internal 3-element direction vector. Allows read/write access to the internal data; lifetime is tied to the DL_Extrusion instance.
requirements: The returned pointer must not be freed or deleted by the caller.
The pointer becomes invalid when the DL_Extrusion object is destroyed or moved out of scope.
Modifying the pointed-to values will modify the DL_Extrusion instance.

functions.name: DL_Extrusion::getDirection
functions.description: Copies the internal direction vector into the caller-provided array.
requirements: dir must be a non-null pointer to an array of at least 3 doubles.
The function writes to dir[0], dir[1], and dir[2].

functions.name: DL_Extrusion::setElevation
functions.description: Sets the elevation value (distance of the entity’s XY plane from the world origin).
requirements: elevation should be a finite double.

functions.name: DL_Extrusion::getElevation
functions.description: Returns the current elevation value.

functions.name: DL_Extrusion::operator=
functions.description: Assignment operator. Deep-copies the source’s direction components and elevation into this object and returns a copy of this object by value. Does not allocate new memory; overwrites existing internal direction values.
requirements: extru must be a valid DL_Extrusion reference.
Self-assignment is supported by the implementation.
The returned object is a by-value copy of the assigned-to object after assignment; typical usage ignores the return value.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::processCodeValuePair
functions.signature: virtual void DL_CreationInterface::processCodeValuePair(unsigned int groupCode, const std::string& groupValue) = 0;
functions.description: Callback invoked for every code/value tuple read from a DXF file. Implementations can handle the complete DXF content by processing these pairs.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses; base class provides no implementation.
groupCode is a DXF group code as read from the file; groupValue is the associated raw string value.
Can be called many times during parsing and from any DXF section.
Implementations should be prepared to receive values in the order they appear in the file.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::endSection
functions.description: Signals that the current DXF section (e.g., entities, tables, blocks) has finished.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
May be called after a sequence of related code/value tuples that form a section.
Implementations should finalize any state associated with the current section.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addLayer
functions.description: Called for every layer encountered in the DXF. Provides the layer's data for creation/registration.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
The provided DL_LayerData describes one layer as parsed; treat it as read-only.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addLinetype
functions.description: Called for every linetype definition encountered in the DXF.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_LinetypeData contains the linetype header data; dash pattern details may arrive via addLinetypeDash calls.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addLinetypeDash
functions.description: Called for each dash element in the current linetype's pattern.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Dashes are provided sequentially for the current linetype after addLinetype and before the next linetype begins.
length represents one dash/space length in drawing units.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addBlock
functions.description: Called for every block definition start. All subsequently added entities belong to this block until endBlock() is called.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
After this call, entities received should be associated with the current block until endBlock() is invoked.
DL_BlockData identifies the block being defined.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::endBlock
functions.description: Ends the current block definition started with addBlock.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Must only be called when a block definition is active (i.e., after a corresponding addBlock).
Implementations should finalize and close the block context.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addTextStyle
functions.description: Called for every text style (STYLE table entry) read from the DXF.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_StyleData contains the style's properties as parsed.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addPoint
functions.description: Called for each POINT entity.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_PointData contains the point coordinates and related data.
Use current attributes and extrusion (if applicable) for this entity.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addLine
functions.description: Called for each LINE entity.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_LineData contains start and end coordinates.
Use current attributes and extrusion (if applicable).

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addXLine
functions.description: Called for each XLINE (construction line) entity.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_XLineData provides base point and direction.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addRay
functions.description: Called for each RAY entity.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_RayData provides base point and direction.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addArc
functions.description: Called for each ARC entity.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_ArcData contains center, radius, and angle span.
Use current attributes and extrusion (if applicable).

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addCircle
functions.description: Called for each CIRCLE entity.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_CircleData contains center and radius.
Use current attributes and extrusion (if applicable).

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addEllipse
functions.description: Called for each ELLIPSE entity.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_EllipseData contains center, axes, ratio, and parameters.
Use current attributes and extrusion (if applicable).

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addPolyline
functions.description: Called at the start of a POLYLINE entity.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Subsequent addVertex calls deliver the vertices of this polyline; sequence ends with endSequence().
Implementations should initialize polyline state on receipt.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addVertex
functions.description: Called for each VERTEX belonging to the current POLYLINE or related entity requiring vertices.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Only valid after a corresponding addPolyline and before endSequence().
Vertices arrive in the order they are defined in the DXF.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addSpline
functions.description: Called for each SPLINE entity definition header.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Control points, fit points, and knots follow via addControlPoint, addFitPoint, and addKnot respectively until entity completion (endEntity or similar).

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addControlPoint
functions.description: Called for each SPLINE control point.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Valid only after an addSpline and before the spline is completed.
Control points are provided in sequence.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addFitPoint
functions.description: Called for each SPLINE fit point.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Valid only after an addSpline and before the spline is completed.
Fit points are provided in sequence.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addKnot
functions.description: Called for each SPLINE knot value.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Valid only after an addSpline and before the spline is completed.
Knots are provided in sequence.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addInsert
functions.description: Called for each INSERT entity (block reference).
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_InsertData identifies the referenced block and placement/scale/rotation.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addTrace
functions.description: Called for each TRACE entity start.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_TraceData provides the trace corner points and related flags.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::add3dFace
functions.description: Called for each 3DFACE entity.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_3dFaceData provides the face's vertices.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addSolid
functions.description: Called for each SOLID entity start.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_SolidData provides the solid's corner points.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addMText
functions.description: Called for each MTEXT (multi-line text) entity.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Additional text fragments up to 250 chars may have been supplied earlier via addMTextChunk and should be combined as needed.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addMTextChunk
functions.description: Provides additional text chunks (up to 250 characters each) for a pending MTEXT entity. These chunks are emitted before the corresponding addMText call.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Chunks arrive before the final addMText for the same MTEXT.
Implementations should buffer these chunks and attach them to the MTEXT as appropriate.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addText
functions.description: Called for each TEXT entity.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_TextData contains insertion point, height, rotation, string, etc.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addArcAlignedText
functions.description: Called for each Arc Aligned Text entity.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_ArcAlignedTextData contains the geometry and text parameters for text along an arc.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addAttribute
functions.description: Called for each block attribute (ATTRIB) entity.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_AttributeData contains tag, value, and placement.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addDimAlign
functions.signature: virtual void DL_CreationInterface::addDimAlign(const DL_DimensionData& data, const DL_DimAlignedData& edata) = 0;
functions.description: Called for each aligned dimension entity.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_DimensionData provides common dimension data; DL_DimAlignedData provides aligned-specific data.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addDimLinear
functions.signature: virtual void DL_CreationInterface::addDimLinear(const DL_DimensionData& data, const DL_DimLinearData& edata) = 0;
functions.description: Called for each linear or rotated dimension entity.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_DimensionData provides common dimension data; DL_DimLinearData provides linear/rotated-specific data.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addDimRadial
functions.signature: virtual void DL_CreationInterface::addDimRadial(const DL_DimensionData& data, const DL_DimRadialData& edata) = 0;
functions.description: Called for each radial dimension entity.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_DimensionData provides common dimension data; DL_DimRadialData provides radial-specific data.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addDimDiametric
functions.signature: virtual void DL_CreationInterface::addDimDiametric(const DL_DimensionData& data, const DL_DimDiametricData& edata) = 0;
functions.description: Called for each diametric dimension entity.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_DimensionData provides common dimension data; DL_DimDiametricData provides diametric-specific data.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addDimAngular
functions.signature: virtual void DL_CreationInterface::addDimAngular(const DL_DimensionData& data, const DL_DimAngular2LData& edata) = 0;
functions.description: Called for each angular dimension entity (two-lines version).
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_DimensionData provides common dimension data; DL_DimAngular2LData provides two-line angular-specific data.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addDimAngular3P
functions.signature: virtual void DL_CreationInterface::addDimAngular3P(const DL_DimensionData& data, const DL_DimAngular3PData& edata) = 0;
functions.description: Called for each angular dimension entity (three-points version).
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_DimensionData provides common dimension data; DL_DimAngular3PData provides three-point angular-specific data.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addDimOrdinate
functions.signature: virtual void DL_CreationInterface::addDimOrdinate(const DL_DimensionData& data, const DL_DimOrdinateData& edata) = 0;
functions.description: Called for each ordinate dimension entity.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_DimensionData provides common dimension data; DL_DimOrdinateData provides ordinate-specific data.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addLeader
functions.description: Called at the start of a LEADER entity.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Subsequent calls to addLeaderVertex provide the vertices of the leader until completion (endSequence or endEntity).

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addLeaderVertex
functions.description: Called for each vertex of the current LEADER entity.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Only valid after a corresponding addLeader and before the leader is completed.
Vertices are provided in sequence.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addHatch
functions.description: Called for each HATCH entity header.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Hatch loops and edges follow via addHatchLoop and addHatchEdge calls until the entity is complete.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addImage
functions.description: Called for each IMAGE entity (raster image reference).
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_ImageData contains insertion, size, clipping, and reference handle information.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::linkImage
functions.description: Called for each IMAGEDEF object, linking image definitions used by IMAGE entities.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
DL_ImageDefData contains image definition (path, size, handle).
Implementations should associate definitions to images by handle as supplied in the DXF.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addHatchLoop
functions.description: Called for each loop in the current HATCH entity.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Valid only after addHatch and before the hatch is completed.
Edges comprising the loop follow via addHatchEdge calls.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addHatchEdge
functions.description: Called for each edge element within the current HATCH loop.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Valid only after a corresponding addHatchLoop and before the end of that loop/hatch.
Edges are provided in sequence to define the loop boundary.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addXRecord
functions.description: Called for each XRecord object with the given handle.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
The handle identifies the XRecord being described; subsequent tuples arrive via addXRecord* calls.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addXRecordString
functions.signature: virtual void DL_CreationInterface::addXRecordString(int code, const std::string& value) = 0;
functions.description: Called for XRecord data tuples of type string.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Must be associated with the current XRecord context as established by addXRecord.
code is the DXF group code for the value.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addXRecordReal
functions.signature: virtual void DL_CreationInterface::addXRecordReal(int code, double value) = 0;
functions.description: Called for XRecord data tuples of type double.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Must be associated with the current XRecord context as established by addXRecord.
code is the DXF group code for the value.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addXRecordInt
functions.signature: virtual void DL_CreationInterface::addXRecordInt(int code, int value) = 0;
functions.description: Called for XRecord data tuples of type int.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Must be associated with the current XRecord context as established by addXRecord.
code is the DXF group code for the value.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addXRecordBool
functions.signature: virtual void DL_CreationInterface::addXRecordBool(int code, bool value) = 0;
functions.description: Called for XRecord data tuples of type bool.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Must be associated with the current XRecord context as established by addXRecord.
code is the DXF group code for the value.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addXDataApp
functions.description: Signals the beginning of an XData section for the specified application ID.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Subsequent XData tuples arrive via addXDataString/addXDataReal/addXDataInt until the XData section ends.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addXDataString
functions.signature: virtual void DL_CreationInterface::addXDataString(int code, const std::string& value) = 0;
functions.description: Called for XData tuples of type string for the current application section.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Valid only after addXDataApp for the current section.
code is the XData group code.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addXDataReal
functions.signature: virtual void DL_CreationInterface::addXDataReal(int code, double value) = 0;
functions.description: Called for XData tuples of type double for the current application section.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Valid only after addXDataApp for the current section.
code is the XData group code.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addXDataInt
functions.signature: virtual void DL_CreationInterface::addXDataInt(int code, int value) = 0;
functions.description: Called for XData tuples of type int for the current application section.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Valid only after addXDataApp for the current section.
code is the XData group code.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addDictionary
functions.description: Called for each DICTIONARY object.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Dictionary entries follow via addDictionaryEntry calls.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::addDictionaryEntry
functions.description: Called for each entry within the current dictionary.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.
Valid only after a corresponding addDictionary and before the dictionary concludes.

functions.name: DL_CreationInterface::endEntity
functions.description: Called after an entity has been completed to signal end-of-entity processing.
requirements: Must be implemented by subclasses.

functions.description: Writes the DXF file terminator (EOF).
requirements: Should be called once after all sections are properly closed.
Derived class must implement dxfString.

functions.name: DL_Writer::comment
functions.description: Writes a DXF 999 comment record with the provided text.
requirements: text must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
Derived class must implement dxfString.

functions.name: DL_Writer::entity
functions.description: Begins a DXF entity by writing its type name. For DXF 2000+, also writes a unique handle using handle().
requirements: entTypeName must be a valid, null-terminated C string naming a DXF entity type (e.g., "LINE", "CIRCLE").
For DXF versions >= DL_VERSION_2000, derived class must implement dxfHex (used via handle()).
Call within an appropriate section (typically ENTITIES or within BLOCKs).

functions.name: DL_Writer::entityAttributes
functions.description: Writes common entity attributes such as layer, color (ACI and optional true color), lineweight, linetype scale, and linetype name, honoring version-specific behavior (e.g., omitting BYLAYER color for R12).
requirements: attrib.getLayer() should return a valid layer name string.
For R12 (version < DL_VERSION_2000), BYLAYER (color 256) is omitted; for >= 2000, color and extended attributes can be written.
Derived class must implement dxfString, dxfInt, and dxfReal.

functions.name: DL_Writer::subClass
functions.description: Writes a 100 subclass marker with the given class name.
requirements: sub must be a valid, null-terminated C string naming a subclass.
Derived class must implement dxfString.

functions.name: DL_Writer::tableLayerEntry
functions.signature: void tableLayerEntry(unsigned long int h = 0) const
functions.description: Writes the start of a LAYER table entry. For DXF 2000+, writes handle and subclass markers for AcDbSymbolTableRecord and AcDbLayerTableRecord, and optionally sets 67 if needed externally (not here).
requirements: Call within a LAYER table in the TABLES section.
If h==0 and version >= DL_VERSION_2000, a unique handle is generated via handle(); if non-zero, it is written as the entry handle in hex.
Derived class must implement dxfString and dxfHex (for DXF 2000+).

functions.name: DL_Writer::tableLinetypeEntry
functions.signature: void tableLinetypeEntry(unsigned long int h = 0) const
functions.description: Writes the start of a LTYPE table entry. For DXF 2000+, writes handle and subclass markers for AcDbSymbolTableRecord and AcDbLinetypeTableRecord.
requirements: Call within an LTYPE table in the TABLES section.
If h==0 and version >= DL_VERSION_2000, a unique handle is generated via handle(); if non-zero, it is written as the entry handle in hex.
Derived class must implement dxfString and dxfHex (for DXF 2000+).

functions.name: DL_Writer::tableAppidEntry
functions.signature: void tableAppidEntry(unsigned long int h = 0) const
functions.description: Writes the start of an APPID table entry. For DXF 2000+, writes handle and subclass markers for AcDbSymbolTableRecord and AcDbRegAppTableRecord.
requirements: Call within an APPID table in the TABLES section.
If h==0 and version >= DL_VERSION_2000, a unique handle is generated via handle(); if non-zero, it is written as the entry handle in hex.
Derived class must implement dxfString and dxfHex (for DXF 2000+).

functions.name: DL_Writer::sectionBlockEntry
functions.signature: void sectionBlockEntry(unsigned long int h = 0) const
functions.description: Writes a BLOCK record start within the BLOCKS section. For DXF 2000+, writes handle, subclass markers, space flag for paper space if applicable, and sets layer to "0".
requirements: Call within the BLOCKS section before the block's contents.
If h==0 and version >= DL_VERSION_2000, a unique handle is generated via handle(); if non-zero, it is written as the record handle in hex.
Derived class must implement dxfString and dxfHex (for DXF 2000+).

functions.name: DL_Writer::sectionBlockEntryEnd
functions.signature: void sectionBlockEntryEnd(unsigned long int h = 0) const
functions.description: Writes an ENDBLK record to end a block within the BLOCKS section. For DXF 2000+, writes handle, subclass markers, optional paper space flag, and sets layer to "0".
requirements: Call within the BLOCKS section after finishing a block's entities.
If h==0 and version >= DL_VERSION_2000, a unique handle is generated via handle(); if non-zero, it is written as the record handle in hex.
Derived class must implement dxfString and dxfHex (for DXF 2000+).

functions.name: DL_Writer::color
functions.description: Writes the entity color (DXF group 62) using AutoCAD Color Index (ACI). 256 typically means BYLAYER.
requirements: col should be a valid ACI value (commonly -1 for BYBLOCK, 0-255, 256 for BYLAYER depending on DXF variant).
Derived class must implement dxfInt.

functions.name: DL_Writer::linetype
functions.description: Writes an entity linetype name (group 6).
requirements: lt must be a valid, null-terminated C string naming a linetype.
Derived class must implement dxfString.

functions.name: DL_Writer::linetypeScale
functions.description: Writes the linetype scale (group 48).
requirements: scale should be a finite real number appropriate for DXF linetype scaling.
Derived class must implement dxfReal.

functions.name: DL_Writer::lineWeight
functions.description: Writes the lineweight in hundredths of millimeters (group 370).
requirements: lw should be a valid DXF lineweight enum value or hundredths of mm as per DXF spec for the target version.
Derived class must implement dxfInt.

functions.name: DL_Writer::coord
functions.signature: void coord(int gc, double x, double y, double z = 0) const
functions.description: Writes a 3D coordinate triplet starting at the given base group code gc (writes gc:x, gc+10:y, gc+20:z).
requirements: gc must be a valid base group code for a coordinate in DXF (e.g., 10, 20, etc.).
x, y, z should be finite real numbers.
Derived class must implement dxfReal.

functions.name: DL_Writer::coordTriplet
functions.signature: void coordTriplet(int gc, const double* value) const
functions.description: Writes a 3D coordinate triplet from a pointer to three doubles, starting at base group code gc, if value is non-null.
requirements: If value is non-null, it must point to at least three valid doubles representing x, y, z in that order.
It is permitted to pass a null pointer; in that case, nothing is written.
Derived class must implement dxfReal.

functions.name: DL_Writer::resetHandle
functions.description: Resets the internal handle counter to 1 for subsequent handle() calls.
requirements: Use with caution to avoid handle collisions in a single DXF stream.
Affects subsequent calls to handle().

functions.name: DL_Writer::handle
functions.description: Writes the current unique handle value in hex using the specified group code (default 5) and increments the internal handle counter. Returns the handle value that was written.
requirements: Derived class must implement dxfHex to perform the write.
Callers may use the return value to reference the written object if needed.
If resetHandle() was called, the sequence restarts, so ensure no duplicates in the output stream.

functions.name: DL_Writer::getNextHandle
functions.description: Returns the next handle value that will be written by handle() without modifying it.
requirements: None beyond object validity. Use to preview or reserve handle values.

functions.name: DL_Writer::dxfReal
functions.signature: virtual void dxfReal(int gc, double value) const = 0
functions.description: Pure virtual low-level write for a real-number DXF group code/value pair. Must be implemented by subclasses to emit output.
requirements: Subclasses must implement this method before any higher-level writer APIs are used.
gc should be a valid DXF real-type group code; value should be a finite real number.

functions.name: DL_Writer::dxfInt
functions.signature: virtual void dxfInt(int gc, int value) const = 0
functions.description: Pure virtual low-level write for an integer DXF group code/value pair. Must be implemented by subclasses to emit output.
requirements: Subclasses must implement this method before any higher-level writer APIs are used.
gc should be a valid DXF integer-type group code.

functions.name: DL_Writer::dxfBool
functions.signature: virtual void dxfBool(int gc, bool value) const
functions.description: Virtual low-level write for a boolean DXF group code/value pair. Default implementation writes as int via dxfInt.
requirements: If the default implementation is used, dxfInt must be implemented by the subclass.
gc should be a valid DXF integer/boolean-type group code.

functions.name: DL_Writer::dxfHex
functions.signature: virtual void dxfHex(int gc, int value) const = 0
functions.description: Pure virtual low-level write for a hexadecimal integer DXF group code/value pair (commonly used for handles). Must be implemented by subclasses to emit output.
requirements: Subclasses must implement this method before features that write handles or hex fields are used.
gc should be a valid DXF hex-type group code.

functions.name: DL_Writer::dxfString
functions.signature: virtual void dxfString(int gc, const char* value) const = 0
functions.description: Pure virtual low-level write for a string DXF group code/value pair from a C string. Must be implemented by subclasses to emit output.
requirements: value must be a valid, null-terminated C string or follow subclass-defined handling for null.
Subclasses must implement this method before higher-level writer APIs are used.

functions.name: DL_Writer::dxfString
functions.signature: virtual void dxfString(int gc, const std::string& value) const = 0
functions.description: Pure virtual low-level write for a string DXF group code/value pair from a std::string. Must be implemented by subclasses to emit output.
requirements: Subclasses must implement this method before higher-level writer APIs are used.

functions.name: DL_WriterA::DL_WriterA
functions.signature: DL_WriterA::DL_WriterA(const char* fname, DL_Codes::version version = DL_VERSION_2000)
functions.description: Constructs an ASCII DXF writer that targets the file specified by fname and initializes it for the given DXF version. Intended to prepare an output stream used by the DL_Writer interface for emitting low-level DXF group codes and values.
requirements: fname must point to a valid, null-terminated C-string path.
fname must not be NULL; the header comments note no handling for NULL or open failures.
The target file path must be creatable/writable by the process; otherwise openFailed() will report failure.
Callers should check openFailed() after constructing the writer before attempting to write.

functions.name: DL_WriterA::~DL_WriterA
functions.description: Destructor for the DXF ASCII writer. Cleans up resources associated with the output stream. Typical usage is to destroy the writer after finishing all DXF output (often after calling close()).
requirements: Object must not be used after destruction.
Behavior regarding implicit close/flush is not documented; callers should prefer calling close() explicitly before destruction when deterministic closure is required.

functions.name: DL_WriterA::openFailed
functions.description: Returns true if the output file failed to open. Use immediately after construction to verify that the target file stream is ready for writing.
requirements: May be called any time after construction.
If this returns true, no writing functions (dxfReal/dxfInt/dxfHex/dxfString) should be called until the issue is resolved (typically by constructing a new writer with a valid path).

functions.name: DL_WriterA::close
functions.description: Closes the underlying ASCII DXF output stream. Call when no further DXF data will be written to ensure all data is flushed and the file handle is released.
requirements: Should be called at most once per writer instance; repeated calls after close are unsupported/unspecified.
After close(), no further dxf* writing functions should be called on this instance.

functions.name: DL_WriterA::dxfReal
functions.signature: void DL_WriterA::dxfReal(int gc, double value) const
functions.description: Writes a DXF real (floating-point) value with the specified DXF group code gc to the ASCII DXF file.
requirements: The writer must have successfully opened the file (openFailed() must return false) and not yet be closed.
gc should be a valid DXF group code for a real value; exact valid ranges depend on the DXF spec (not documented here).
No exceptions or error codes are documented; callers should ensure preconditions to avoid I/O errors.

functions.name: DL_WriterA::dxfInt
functions.signature: void DL_WriterA::dxfInt(int gc, int value) const
functions.description: Writes a DXF integer value with the specified DXF group code gc to the ASCII DXF file.
requirements: The writer must have successfully opened the file (openFailed() must return false) and not yet be closed.
gc should be a valid DXF group code for an integer value; exact valid ranges depend on the DXF spec (not documented here).

functions.name: DL_WriterA::dxfHex
functions.signature: void DL_WriterA::dxfHex(int gc, int value) const
functions.description: Writes a DXF value formatted as hexadecimal with the specified DXF group code gc to the ASCII DXF file. Typically used for handles or color values that are represented in hex in DXF.
requirements: The writer must have successfully opened the file (openFailed() must return false) and not yet be closed.
gc should be a valid DXF group code for a hexadecimal-formatted value; exact applicability depends on the DXF spec (not documented here).
Acceptable range/format of value is not specified; callers should use values appropriate for the intended DXF field (unknown from this header).

functions.name: DL_WriterA::dxfString
functions.signature: void DL_WriterA::dxfString(int gc, const char* value) const
functions.description: Writes a DXF string value with the specified DXF group code gc to the ASCII DXF file. This overload accepts a C-string.
requirements: The writer must have successfully opened the file (openFailed() must return false) and not yet be closed.
value must be a valid, non-null, null-terminated C-string.
gc should be a valid DXF group code for a string value; exact valid ranges depend on the DXF spec (not documented here).

functions.name: DL_WriterA::strReplace
functions.signature: static void DL_WriterA::strReplace(char* str, char src, char dest)
functions.description: In-place utility to replace all occurrences of character src with character dest in the provided C-string. Useful for normalizing strings before writing to DXF.
requirements: str must be a valid, non-null pointer to a mutable, null-terminated C-string.
The memory pointed to by str must be writable; the function modifies the buffer in place.
Behavior is undefined if str is not null-terminated.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::DL_Dxf

functions.name: DL_Dxf::readDxfGroups

functions.name: DL_Dxf::getStrippedLine

functions.name: DL_Dxf::stripWhiteSpace
functions.signature: static bool DL_Dxf::stripWhiteSpace(char** s, bool stripSpaces = true)
functions.description: Strips whitespace (and optionally spaces) from a C-string in-place by adjusting the pointer and/or contents.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::processDXFGroup
functions.signature: bool DL_Dxf::processDXFGroup(DL_CreationInterface* creationInterface, int groupCode, const std::string& groupValue)
functions.description: Processes a single DXF group code/value pair, updating internal state or emitting entities via the creation interface.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addSetting
functions.description: Emits the current parsed DXF setting (e.g., $ACADVER) through the creation interface.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addLayer
functions.description: Emits a parsed LAYER table entry to the creation interface.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addLinetype
functions.description: Emits a parsed LINETYPE table entry to the creation interface.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.
Should be called after required linetype fields (name, pattern, etc.) are parsed.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addBlock
functions.description: Starts a new BLOCK definition based on the currently parsed BLOCK record.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.
Call when a BLOCK record header has been fully parsed.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::endBlock
functions.description: Emits an ENDBLK to close the current block definition.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addTextStyle
functions.description: Emits a parsed text STYLE table entry via the creation interface.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.
Call after parsing all required text style attributes (name, font, flags).

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addPoint
functions.description: Emits a POINT entity with the currently parsed attributes and geometry.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.
Coordinates for the point must have been parsed prior to calling.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addLine
functions.description: Emits a LINE entity using previously parsed start/end coordinates and attributes.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.
Start and end points must be available in internal state.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addXLine
functions.description: Emits an XLINE (infinite line) entity using parsed base point and direction.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addRay
functions.description: Emits a RAY entity defined by parsed base point and direction.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.
Base point and direction vector must be available.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addPolyline
functions.description: Starts a POLYLINE/LWPOLYLINE entity using parsed header data. Subsequent vertices are added with addVertex.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.
Polyline header fields (flags, vertex count, etc.) should be parsed before calling.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addVertex
functions.description: Emits a VERTEX for the current POLYLINE/LWPOLYLINE being constructed.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.
A polyline context must be active before adding vertices.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addSpline
functions.description: Emits a SPLINE entity using parsed spline data (knots, control points, fit points, weights).
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.
Required spline data must be parsed and buffered.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addArc
functions.description: Emits an ARC entity with parsed center, radius, and start/end angles.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.
Center, radius, and angles must be available.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addCircle
functions.description: Emits a CIRCLE entity with parsed center and radius.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.
Center and radius must be available.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addEllipse
functions.description: Emits an ELLIPSE entity using parsed center, major axis, ratio, and angles.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.
Ellipse parameters must be available.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addInsert
functions.description: Emits an INSERT entity (block reference) using parsed block name, insertion point, scale, and rotation.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.
Referenced block must have been defined earlier in the DXF for validity.
Insertion parameters must be available.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addTrace
functions.description: Emits a TRACE entity using parsed corner points.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.
All required TRACE points must be parsed.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::add3dFace
functions.description: Emits a 3DFACE entity using parsed corner points and visibility flags.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.
3DFACE vertex coordinates must be available.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addSolid
functions.description: Emits a SOLID entity using parsed vertex data.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.
Solid vertices must be available.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addMText
functions.description: Emits an MTEXT entity using parsed text content, formatting, and location.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.
MTEXT content and positioning data must be parsed.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addText
functions.description: Emits a TEXT entity using parsed text, position, height, and style.

TEXT fields must be available (string, position, height).

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addArcAlignedText
functions.description: Emits an ARCALIGNEDTEXT entity if present, using parsed arc and text parameters.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.
Arc-aligned text parameters must be parsed.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addAttribute
functions.description: Emits an ATTRIB entity, typically following an INSERT, using parsed tag, value, and positioning.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.
Attribute data must be parsed.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::getDimData

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addDimLinear
functions.description: Emits a linear dimension using parsed dimension data and linear-specific fields.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addDimAligned

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addDimRadial
functions.description: Emits a radial dimension using parsed data referencing a circle/arc.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addDimDiametric
functions.description: Emits a diametric dimension using parsed data associated with a circle/arc.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addDimAngular
functions.description: Emits a two-line angular dimension using parsed references and angles.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addDimAngular3P

requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addDimOrdinate
functions.description: Emits an ordinate dimension using parsed origin and feature location.
requirements: creationInterface must be non-null.
Ordinate dimension data must be available.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addLeader
functions.description: Emits a LEADER entity using parsed leader vertices and flags.

Leader vertices and settings must be parsed.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addHatch
functions.description: Starts or emits a HATCH entity using parsed hatch parameters (pattern/solid, scale, angle).

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addImage

Image entity parameters must be available.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addImageDef

Image definition parameters (file path, width/height) must be available.

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addComment

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addDictionary

functions.name: DL_Dxf::addDictionaryEntry

functions.name: DL_Dxf::handleXRecordData

def rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-./\\:()[]{}#@!$%+.,;~^|"
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def rand_unicodeish(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    choices: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(n):
        pick = rng.randint(0, 5)
        if pick <= 2:
            choices.append(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits))
        elif pick == 3:
            choices.append(chr(rng.choice([0x00E9, 0x00E4, 0x00F6, 0x00FC, 0x00DF])))
        elif pick == 4:
            choices.append(chr(rng.randint(0x03B1, 0x03C9)))
        else:
            choices.append(chr(rng.randint(0x4E00, 0x9FA5)))
    return "".join(choices)


def base_ends_with_sep(p: str) -> bool:
    return p.endswith("/") or p.endswith("\\")


def rand_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    bases = ["/tmp", "/var/tmp", "C:/tmp", "C:/Users/User", "./", "../data"]
    base = rng.choice(bases)
    if rng.choice([True, False]) and not base_ends_with_sep(base):
        base = base + "/"
    name = rand_ascii(rng, 1, 12).replace(" ", "_")
    ext = rng.choice([".png", ".jpg", ".tif", ".bmp", ".dxf", ".shx", ".ttf", ".txt"]) if rng.random() < 0.8 else ""
    return base + name + ext


def build_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    corpus: List[str] = []

    fixed = STATIC_POOL[:]
    rng.shuffle(fixed)
    corpus.extend(fixed[:30])

    corpus.extend([
        "$LTSCALE", "BYLAYER", "BYBLOCK", "Continuous", "HIDDEN",
        "APP", "XR", "IMG", "DCT",
    ])

    for _ in range(10):
        corpus.append(rand_ascii(rng, 1, rng.randint(4, 24)))
    for _ in range(6):
        corpus.append(rand_unicodeish(rng, 2, rng.randint(4, 16)))

    for _ in range(6):
        corpus.append(rand_path(rng))

    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        corpus.append(rand_ascii(rng, 100, 300))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        corpus.append(rand_unicodeish(rng, 50, 200))

    corpus.extend(["", "0", "256", "-3", "0x00FFFFFF", "420", "62", "370", "48", "5"])

    seen = set()
    unique: List[str] = []
    for s in corpus:
        if s not in seen:
            unique.append(s)
            seen.add(s)

    return unique


def pack_null_separated(strings: List[str], limit: int) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    total = 0
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
        need = len(b) + 1
        if total + need > limit:
            break
        parts.append(b)
        parts.append(b"\x00")
        total += need
    if not parts:
        return b"\x00"
    return b"".join(parts)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    strings = build_corpus(rng)
    blob = pack_null_separated(strings, MAX_TOTAL)
    return blob
